chapter, first pass — the energy view instead of force balances.
two equivalent routes to dynamics: Newton–Euler (forces and frames,
painful bookkeeping) vs Lagrangian (kinetic + potential energy in generalized
choose generalized coordinates q; kinetic energy is quadratic in
q̇, so it factors into a mass matrix M(q) — configuration-dependent inertia.
Euler–Lagrange with generalized forces: the ∂KE/∂q terms are where
Coriolis and centrifugal effects come from. They fall out of the derivative,
because M depends on q, the same joint torque accelerates the arm
differently depending on pose. This is why controller gains tuned at one
gravity enters through the potential energy only — V(q), take
partials, done. Gravity is the one term you get for free.
